Safe (0 to 4.4 ppm): Service Home Heaters Annually: Inspect furnaces, water heaters, and gas appliances to ensure safe operation.
Test CO Detectors Monthly: Check batteries and functionality of carbon monoxide alarms on every home level.
Maintain Vehicle Exhaust Systems: Ensure mufflers and tailpipes are free of rust holes or leaks.
Ventilate Workshops Properly: Always use adequate exhaust fans when operating combustion tools in garages.
Inspect Chimneys Regularly: Keep flues clear of soot or bird nests before lighting any wood fires.
Use Electric Appliances Where Possible: Opt for electric or induction stoves to eliminate combustion risks.
Store Fuel Safely: Keep gasoline and propane tanks stored in detached sheds away from living quarters.
Organize Community Safety Audits: Help elderly neighbors inspect their home heating and CO alarm systems.
Promote Fire Safety Education: Partner with local fire departments to distribute home safety guidelines.
Advocate for Building Safety Codes: Support strict municipal inspection requirements for multi-family rental housing.
Moderate (4.5 to 9.4 ppm): Check Appliance Ventilation: Verify that gas stove vents and furnace flues are drawing exhaust properly.
Never Idle in Confined Spaces: Avoid letting vehicle engines run inside attached garages even for a moment.
Increase Indoor Ventilation: Open windows periodically when using gas-powered equipment or heaters.
Monitor Fuel-Burning Equipment: Inspect portable generators or space heaters for signs of incomplete combustion.
Limit Heavy Traffic Exposure: Avoid exercising directly alongside heavy traffic corridors during rush hours.
Inspect Fireplace Dampers: Ensure fireplace flues are fully open before burning any wood or solid fuel.
Test Alarm Sensor Levels: Verify that carbon monoxide detectors are active and sensitive to low-level rises.
Coordinate Neighborhood Awareness Drives: Inform residents about the risks of portable generator placement during storms.
Offer Free Detector Checks: Partner with local community groups to supply fresh batteries for carbon monoxide alarms.
Establish Vehicle Inspection Checkpoints: Support local campaigns offering free tailpipe emissions testing.
Dangerous (9.5+ ppm): Evacuate Immediately If Alarms Sound: Leave the building instantly and call emergency services if CO alarms trigger.
Shut Off Fuel Sources Safely: Turn off gas valves or extinguish fuel appliances if safe to do so before evacuating.
Seek Fresh Air Instantly: Move anyone experiencing dizziness or headaches to an outdoor open-air environment.
Never Use Charcoal Indoors: Avoid bringing grills, hibachis, or camp stoves inside homes, tents, or garages.
Do Not Heat Homes with Ovens: Never use gas kitchen ranges or ovens to heat living spaces.
Keep Generators Outdoors: Operate portable gas generators at least 20 feet away from windows and doors.
Avoid Congested Traffic Tunnels: Refrain from walking or driving through poorly ventilated underground structures.
Deploy Emergency Response Teams: Coordinate local emergency services to inspect buildings with elevated CO readings.
Issue Public Safety Broadcasts: Work with local authorities to broadcast urgent shelter and evacuation warnings.
Provide Emergency Medical Support: Organize community medical response stations for individuals affected by toxic exposure.
